cards.explanation: The answer is sorrowful and deeply distressed. Jesus begins to be sorrowful and deeply distressed. This is a heavy moment, so I'll say it plain. Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, and the two sons of Zebedee are right there to see it.

The answer is to stay and keep watch with Him. Jesus says, “Stay here and keep watch with Me.” It's a simple ask, friends. He doesn't ask them to fix anything, only to stay and keep watch with Him. I think that says a lot about the moment.

The answer is False. Jesus does pray, “…if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me.” Then He finishes with, “Yet not as I will, but as You will.” His own will doesn't come first, and the Father's will does. That's what the text says.

The answer is sleeping. Jesus comes back and finds them sleeping. Before we judge them, friends, let's ask ourselves when we last stared down a heavy eyelid and lost. The text says in a moment that their eyes were heavy (Matthew 26:43).

The reason is that the spirit is willing, but the body is weak. Jesus says, “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.” Anyone who has ever meant to get up early and then hit snooze knows exactly what that is. He speaks it plainly, and it's good to hear.
The answer is False. Jesus returns and finds them sleeping again, “…for their eyes were heavy.” So He doesn't find them awake and watching. That's what the text says.

The words are third and same. Jesus goes away once more and prays a third time, “…saying the same thing.” His first prayer was in verse 39 and the second time was in verse 42, so this is three trips away to pray, and the text keeps count. The text gives no new words this time, and His earlier prayer ended with “…may Your will be done.” (Matthew 26:42).

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!” He tells them to get up first, and then He points out that the betrayer is coming. The scene is about to change fast.

The answer is a large crowd with swords and clubs. Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives “…accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs…” The text says they were sent from the chief priests and elders of the people. He didn't come alone.
The answer is True. The crowd was “…sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.” The text tells us exactly who sent them, friends. It's the leaders of Israel behind this.

The signal was the One he kisses. Judas told the crowd, “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.” A kiss was the signal, and it had been arranged ahead of time. That's what the text says, and it's a heavy detail.
The word is Friend. “‘Friend,’ Jesus replied, ‘do what you came for.’” He answers Judas with that word right after the kiss. Then the men step forward and arrest Him.

The answer is False. One of Jesus' companions draws his sword and strikes the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear. So someone with Jesus does try to fight back. It happens right as the men seize Him.
The answer is True. Jesus tells the companion, “Put your sword back in its place…” and then explains, “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.” He answers him directly.

The answer is more than twelve legions of angels. Jesus says He can call on His Father, and the Father will at once put at His disposal more than twelve legions of angels. A legion is a big group, and He says more than twelve of them. That's the help He says is one call away.

The reason is that Scripture says it must happen this way. Jesus asks, “But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?” He's the One who can call on the angels, and He doesn't. Later He adds, “But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” (Matthew 26:56)

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.” He points that out to the crowd, friends. They came with swords and clubs, but He had been right there teaching in the open.
The word is deserted. The text says, “Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.” I think this one hurts, so I won't dress it up. It's right there in the passage, as the last line of the scene.
